title: Walk to the ghost at up to 0.15 m/s: the destination_v29 locomotion model
summary: Starting from destination_v9 (PR 88), a speed curriculum on Spark taught the policy to walk at up to 0.15 m/s in every direction (destination_v25), and a 600-update Spark fine-tune taught it to stop, stand still and turn in place again while paying the ghost gap at each run's end (destination_v29). On the surrogate suite the destination_v29 update-600 checkpoint passes all 13 learning probes and every walk and walk-then-stop case in 8 directions at 0.05 to 0.15 m/s with no fall; v9 passes 3, 0 and 0 of 8 walks at 0.1, 0.125 and 0.15 m/s. Its 0.05 m/s walks end 2.47 mm (median) from the ghost, against 0.82 mm for v9, and it holds about 18 mm of lag at 0.15 m/s. Of the 96 required cases it passes 53 on the surrogate, against v9's 16 natively: it misses every case at 0.20 m/s or faster, the tight 0.4 rad/s arcs, the -0.4 rad/s turn in place, three of the eight walk-and-turn cases, one gentle arc, one segment of the transition program and the formal cases at 0 and 0.16 m/s on body tilt. The native evaluator cannot yet run its ghost_v11 inputs or speed-scaled gait clock, so all evaluation so far is on the surrogate.
next: Teach the native evaluator the ghost_v11 inputs and the speed-scaled gait clock and run the 96 required cases natively on the destination_v29 update-600 checkpoint with unchanged thresholds; then train turning while walking and faster turns (tight 0.4 rad/s arcs, combined walk-and-turn cases).
